concepts.title: Habitat and Abiotic Factors
concepts.definition: Every organism lives in a habitat that supplies food, shelter and mates, and the habitat is shaped by four major abiotic components: temperature, water, light and soil, together with the physico-chemical features of the substratum and atmosphere.
concepts.key_idea: Ecology at the organism level is basically the study of how an organism meets the stresses these abiotic factors impose.
concepts.textbook_ref: lebo111.txt unit introduction, habitat definition and abiotic factor sections

solution_steps.explain: temperature, water, light and soil are identified as the major abiotic components
the organism's response to these factors defines its distribution on earth
habitat is the place with a particular set of biotic and abiotic components an organism lives in

concepts.title: Responses to Abiotic Stress
concepts.definition: Organisms cope with unfavourable temperature and water conditions in four ways: regulate internal conditions (homeostasis like mammals and birds), simply conform to the ambient conditions, migrate temporarily to more suitable habitats, or suspend activity (diapause, hibernation, aestivation).
concepts.key_idea: Only a small fraction of animals are true regulators; most are conformers because thermoregulation is energetically expensive.

solution_steps.explain: regulate, conform, migrate and suspend are the four textbook responses
the desert lizard's body temperature drifts with ambient temperature, so it conforms

concepts.title: Population Growth Models
concepts.definition: Population density changes through natality, mortality, immigration and emigration; under unlimited resources growth is exponential (dN/dt = rN) while under the carrying capacity K of real habitats growth is logistic (dN/dt = rN(K-N)/K), giving a sigmoid curve.
concepts.key_idea: The term (K-N)/K weights growth down as N approaches carrying capacity, so computing it tells how much room a population still has to grow.
concepts.textbook_ref: lebo111.txt population growth equations and sigmoid curve section

solution_steps.explain: the fraction (K-N)/K equals 1 at tiny N and 0 at N = K
exponential growth dN/dt equals r times N

concepts.title: Population Interactions
concepts.definition: Populations of different species interact as mutualism (both benefit), competition (both harmed), predation and parasitism (one benefits, other harmed), commensalism (one benefits, other unaffected) and amensalism (one harmed, other unaffected).
concepts.key_idea: Competition is best defined as a minus-minus interaction and its outcome may be competitive exclusion or resource partitioning (like the five closely related species of warblers on a single tree).
